# Native existing-checkpoint handoff fixture

GitHub CI only. `node tests/evidence-legacy-adoption-ui.cjs --prepare-only` performs local static/source preparation without launching a browser or a server. Native execution requires the approved CI environment and routes a fixed synthetic HTTPS origin entirely to pinned repository bytes. No production entrypoint imports this fixture.

## What is real, and what is synthetic

`old.html` starts with explicitly synthetic completed chapter-9 story prerequisites and a phase-2 finale envelope that has **no checkpoint**. Earlier campaign play is not claimed. Its arbitrary points, daily text, operations counters/input/seed and unrelated sentinel strings are declared test data. Unchanged `field-model.js`, `field-missions.js`, `field-art.js` and `chapter-space.js` are loaded from actual hash-pinned files. A trusted Resume and WAIT click causes the original controller and the original chapter-space save closure to write a genuine partial checkpoint. The writer page closes before the cold realm reads final native localStorage bytes. Native modifiers are genuinely empty; nonempty saved-modifier fixed-point coverage is portable only.

The cold realm archives exactly the selected 12 strings and absence, then publishes a separate deterministic checkpoint owner. It loads no original legacy, reward, daily, cloud, storage, app or chapter-space writer. A narrow read-only canonical facade permits only the byte-identical current-chapter `9` no-op. The original Field controller receives the owner-selected checkpoint. One trusted WAIT is frozen synchronously; initial and recursive stop saves are quarantined/compared. A real timer save before WAIT retains its exact state and blocks the experiment, even if floating-point increment leaves its numeric value unchanged. A distinct save or original callback exception cancels publication. The two explicit callback-corruption cases are synthetic negative tests, not earned gameplay.

Persistence starts only after the successful outer original callback returns. The source archive and next archive are independently sealed/read back before their selecting owner revisions. Original source bytes are never rewritten. Fresh realms validate archived dependencies, use localStorage solely as an exact drift guard, and restore revision 1 through the actual controller twice. No completion, award, daily action, queue effect, pacing change or external network request occurs.

## Explicit test-only lifecycle fence

A paused original controller still receives blur, visibility and pagehide saves. This host therefore **changes lifecycle timing**: while owner persistence is active or the adapter has physical/retained unresolved work, it defers entry into the original blur, visibilitychange, pagehide and native interval callbacks. There is at most one pending callback for each of those four types. The original callback's first `this`/arguments are retained only in its own realm and epoch; these original callbacks do not inspect event arguments, whose DOM `currentTarget` may already be reset when drained.

After all asynchronous leases and adapter work drain, pending callbacks run once under the original-controller workspace reservation against the already-paused/inactive controller. Each pending slot is cleared before invocation. Stale-epoch, invalidated or blocked realms never drain into a new identity. Input remains fenced. This is a cooperative fixture barrier, not a production lock or protection against an uncooperative old tab. The interval itself uses real native time and unchanged cadence; no clock or model action is faked.

## Representation budget and observations

The implementation reuses the unchanged PhaseBudget with 393,216 adapter bytes, 32,768 metadata bytes, and an additional 32,768-byte bridge charge under the 1,016,832 joint ceiling. The accepted source bundle is at most 65,536 framed bytes; checkpoint admission is 7,680 bytes initially and 8,192 after WAIT. Source capture reserves its full source lease before the first native read. Every guard/collector read owns one 65,536-byte native-read slot and validates/transfers the result before releasing it. Cloud and attribution markers are rejected one at a time, without retaining their non-null strings. Original restore/action/recursive saves keep a 327,680-byte workspace through the outer callback; quiescent controller retention persists for the realm lifetime. Pinned mechanic-11 scene output is checked at 20,480 UTF16 bytes and four renders per realm.

This is an encoded-representation schedule, **not whole-fixture heap/RSS or native/browser memory measurement**. Separately excluded instrumentation is bounded: 4,096 events, 20,000 compact budget observations, 2,048 transport summaries, 32,768 native transaction events, 12,000 native-storage observations and 64 input rows. Report/test-runner copies, DOM/layout, static source/assets, engine deserialization, arbitrary initial native `getItem` materialization and GC are excluded. Before each full snapshot, actual JSON-UTF16 bytes are reported per retained observation array and checked against a separate 64 MiB aggregate limit; its observation snapshot copy has the same separate limit. Held-state immutable-candidate/diagnostic observations are explicitly excluded instrumentation. The JSON result artifact has a separate 16 MiB limit. Original `MKTYField.snapshot()` inspection runs under a workspace reservation only after asynchronous work drains; unresolved held-commit observations expose only the immutable captured checkpoint and diagnostics.

Numeric foreign account/queue names may be inspected, but operation/controller code never reads their values. Independent verifier-only reads confirm their exact sentinel bytes. Unsupported or unattributed pending-key families block. All seven cloud metadata keys and legacy attribution must be absent.

## Failure evidence and limits

The native matrix covers staging/readback/selecting-record cuts, actual abort after request success, held native completion plus real watchdog outcome-unknown and exact retry, bounded deferred lifecycle callbacks, timer-before-WAIT, boot and recursive-save quarantine, same-principal contention, source/epoch drift with read-only reconciliation, missing dependency, reserve refusal and genuine native QuotaExceededError. Quota uses a fresh disposable disk-backed profile, a real no-write cache-expiry wait, explicit override/reset evidence and bounded confirmed-close cleanup. An injected abort or logical quota cannot substitute for a native QuotaExceededError.

Native evidence proves one closed-realm checkpoint handoff and graceful reloads. It does not prove a fully earned campaign, signed/server reward authority, migration of real players, cloud merge, production routing, old-client exclusion, power-loss durability, eviction/site-data survival, physical Telegram behavior or a lossless rollback to old JavaScript. Portable owner tests separately cover differing fixed-head contenders.
